images.inspection: Opened entire actual file with original detail at its native pixel dimensions; compared selected originals, models and corresponding drawn staging.

findings.identity_and_proportions: Neet has a full narrow tan trunk, fine tall legs, projecting cream muzzle and broad triangular ears in quarter profile. Buddy has a continuous charcoal trunk extending behind his frontal chest, substantial leg shafts, real clearance and a modest furnished head. Perspective shortens Buddy without turning him into a square terrier.
findings.anatomy_limb_ownership_support: Neet has four independently traceable grounded legs; his near hind leg bends into a full thigh. Buddy forelegs are separate; far hind leg is occluded behind Neet, while the visible hind foot belongs to Buddy. Three seated visitors have separate front paws and haunches. Shadows and paving establish a shared ground plane; no floating or merged body.
findings.grooming_and_tail: Neet flank contains shallow, nondirectional paint loops also visible in courtyard stone/wall; the outline remains close and the neck shading does not project a long ruff. Buddy torso has close mottling distinct from the long directional pale ear/muzzle furnishings. His dark tail is slender, gently lowered from rump, with modest edge fringe, not a plume or ring. Neet nub is very short.
findings.perspective_scene_and_historical_setting: Three patient visitors sit at the open gate opposite standing Neet; Buddy is forward of the cropped human and crates. This fits the greeting before Heather lifts Neet. Modest courtyard, crates and village lane fit the historical Heather-centered arrival; no additional named human or later household imported.
findings.comedy_continuity_finish: The seated audience and solemn little sentry make the warning disproportionate; Buddy open, friendly expression contrasts with Neet. Five separate silhouettes remain readable. Warm restrained finish has clean scene edges, no accidental text or conspicuous artifact. Human clothing/partial leg remains provisional.

findings.identity_and_proportions: Upright Neet has a full narrow torso, long fine straight forelegs, folded rear legs, a tiny visible nub, projecting pale muzzle and pointed cupped ears shown mostly in profile. Buddy remains a full charcoal body with pale thigh/foot and visible furnished muzzle under cloth.
findings.anatomy_limb_ownership_support: Buddy back runs continuously from rump at left into the shoulder/neck beneath blanket at right; muzzle emerges at the anatomically plausible curled neck end. The visible near thigh folds into hock and paw in front of rump. Far limbs are reasonably hidden by body/cloth. Blanket is supported by the head/shoulder and contacts folded base; it is neither a disconnected head nor a hovering sheet. Neet two forefeet and folded rear support sit on tiled floor.
findings.grooming_and_tail: Actual v002 has close smooth outer trunk shapes. Remaining internal fine nondirectional looping is a paint/paper pattern repeated on wall/tile, without the directional shoulder tuft field seen in staging. Buddy pale thigh and hidden ear maintain regional furnishing; dark curled tail at left remains narrow and does not become a plume. Neet does not acquire long neck strands or expanded ruff volume.
findings.perspective_scene_and_historical_setting: Low sill lets seated Neet look through remaining curtain gap without impossible elevation. Buddy has tucked head under one corner of his floor blanket. Cropped Heather foot at far right is plausible; her later hand stroke has not been prematurely pictured. Warm room/cool evening street convey homecoming without changing household.
findings.comedy_continuity_finish: Neet elects to keep seeing while Buddy deliberately sees nothing, clearly conveyed by opposite head orientations and blanket concealment. Quiet composition leaves the spoken final payoff for the following text. Connected resting anatomy and restrained light make an earned close; no garbled lettering, extra paws or edge contamination.

historical_reconsideration.assessment: Earlier rejection and later reversal were both read. This is a new direct inspection against photographs and the expanded close-coat rule, not deference to accepted sibling artwork. Low-relief nondirectional texture shared with inanimate surfaces is distinguishable here from actual long fur strands or enlarged silhouette. Acceptance is for the pinned actual image, not a blanket permission for textured coats.
